leading_positions.synthesis: All five name targeted protein degradation (B067) as their preferred single prize part, and five is the majority threshold in this committee. Four of them (Aili, Aqvist, Linke, Zou) propose the same laureates, Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with citations built on bifunctional PROTAC molecules directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system to a chosen protein. Chabes keeps Crews and Deshaies but names Handa instead of Ciulli, and frames the citation more broadly as turning ubiquitin-proteasome chemistry into a design principle that covers both PROTACs and glues. What is shared is the principle (event-driven removal rather than inhibition), independent reproduction, and the same stated reservations: no approved degrader is cited and the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim) is not covered by a PROTAC-only trio. What is not shared is the third name, whether the citation should reach the glue branch, and how much weight the clinical-maturity point should carry. Brzezinski, Somfai and Sparr do not prefer B067, although each lists it as an alternative (Brzezinski and Somfai as first alternative, Sparr as first alternative), so the five-member count is of stated first preferences only.

Somfai alone prefers palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) on grounds of maturity, wide routine use and a clean two-person credit, with B067 and B022 as alternatives. Linke lists B013 as second alternative and Zou says he ranked it fifth, and both call it an honest but incremental extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Chabes and Aqvist describe the novelty margin over 2010 as thin, while Somfai answers that C-N bond formation required its own ligand and mechanistic work. Kosugi is noted as a precedence footnote by Somfai and Zou, and Somfai flags that this rests on his recollection.

Sparr alone prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen), as a physical-chemical organizing principle with a quantitative base. She states plainly that her own field makes her generous and that in-cell phase separation versus overexpression artefacts is unresolved. Linke (who listed B049 as first alternative) and the other members who commented (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai, Zou) all raise the same artefact and physiological-relevance concern; none of them prefers it as the lead. The shared view is that the weakness bears on the wording of any citation, and the open disagreement is whether it also bears on readiness this year, and whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag should stand beside Hyman and Brangwynne.

Brzezinski alone proposes a two-part prize: long-range electron tunneling in proteins (Gray, Winkler) and base editing (Liu alone), with B067 and B036 as alternatives. He accepts that pairing unrelated achievements is a weaker story than a single unified one and that B067 may be stronger if its attribution can be settled. Aqvist and Zou question whether B069 is separable from the Marcus prize of 1992, and Aili and Sparr share concern that base editing sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize. No other member lists B069 as a preference or alternative in the round-1 files.

areas_of_agreement: B067 has the broadest explicit round-1 support: five of eight members prefer it, and two more (Brzezinski, Somfai) list it as their first alternative, while Sparr lists it as first alternative as well.

All members who discuss B067 describe the same core principle: a small molecule recruits an E3 ligase to a chosen protein so that the target is removed rather than inhibited, and the principle has been independently reproduced.
Crews and Deshaies are named by every member who proposes laureates for B067, so the concept-origin credit is not contested among proposers.
All members who comment on B067 flag the same two reservations: no approved degrader drug is cited, and the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands do not fit a three-name prize without a cut.
Members who discuss B049 agree that the founding liquid-like droplet observations are real and influential, and that the physiological claims for in-cell condensates are not settled.
B013 is treated by its supporters and critics alike as the safest candidate for maturity and attribution (Buchwald and Hartwig), with the open issue being novelty relative to the 2010 prize.
scientific_disputes: Whether many reported cellular condensates are true thermodynamic phase separation or overexpression and in vitro artefacts, and whether that undermines B049 as a prize or only its citation wording (Sparr, Linke, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou, Somfai, Aili).
Whether C-N coupling (B013) is a new bond-forming achievement distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize or an extension of it (Somfai against Aqvist, Aili, Chabes, Linke, Zou).

Whether Gray and Winkler's work (B069) is a separable experimental and biological achievement or a continuation of the electron-transfer theory recognised in 1992 (Brzezinski against Aqvist, Chabes, Zou).

Whether the PROTAC concept is the generalizable chemistry to reward or whether the cereblon and glue mechanism is the more fundamental advance (Aili, Aqvist, Zou for the former; Chabes, with Handa, for the latter).
Aili questions how much of degrader chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimization around an existing biological mechanism, while Linke, Aqvist and Zou regard it as a new design principle.
attribution_disputes: B067 third laureate: Ciulli (Aili, Aqvist, Linke, Zou) versus Handa (Chabes); Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are named as excluded contributors with serious claims by several members.

Whether PROTACs and thalidomide-type molecular glues are one achievement or two, and if two, whether a two-part prize would force one of the PROTAC names out to keep within three laureates (Chabes, Brzezinski, Zou, Aqvist).
B049: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen (Sparr) versus giving the physical-chemistry side to Pappu or Mittag, with the three-person cut contested (Sparr, Brzezinski).
B013: Buchwald and Hartwig are described as a clean pair, with Kosugi as a precedence footnote (Somfai, Zou).

B047 and B029 are described as having diffuse credit (Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer; Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok, Kanatzidis), and Aqvist and Zou disagree on whether Grätzel belongs in a perovskite trio.
maturity_disputes: Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B067 premature in 2026; Zou states he is uncertain of the current clinical status, and Aili, Aqvist and Zou do not think it should decide the matter.
Whether B049 is ready given unresolved physiological relevance, versus the clinical-outcome risk that applies to B067 (Aqvist, Sparr, Linke).
Whether base editing (B052) is too close to the 2020 CRISPR prize or too early for long-term clinical outcomes (Brzezinski, Chabes, Aili, Sparr).
Whether the committee should prefer a mature, validated method (B013) over a younger principle with greater novelty (Somfai against Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Aili).
Perovskite stability and lead toxicity are described as open by Aqvist, Somfai and Zou, so B029 is judged premature by those who comment.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski discloses that his research on respiratory proton and electron transfer is scientifically adjacent to Gray and Winkler (B069), and asks the committee to judge whether recusal is needed.
Sparr discloses that her research on lipid self-assembly and amyloid is scientifically close to B049 and B047, and describes this as field bias, not a recusal matter.

Zou discloses that B022 and B029 lie close to her or his own field of zeolites and porous materials with no collaboration with the named candidates, and notes he is the only supporter of B022 in the opening round.
Somfai discloses a disciplinary bias toward B013 from his Masamune lineage and synthetic methodology interest, with no personal tie to any candidate.
Chabes notes a mild interest in base editing and sequencing as nucleic-acid tools; Aili notes scientific overlap with Sparr on peptide and lipid self-assembly; neither reports a recusal matter.

Sparr and Linke are both from Lund, as is Somfai; Sparr states she does not want agreement between the Lund members to count as independent confirmation. Linke is the chair and a physicist, and notes that his own earlier first-place candidate was B049.
Aqvist, Aili, Chabes and Linke each report no specific conflict with any B067 candidate.
questions_for_round2: Are PROTACs and thalidomide-type molecular glues one achievement or two for citation purposes, and can a single citation phrased around hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system be defended in both branches without claiming more than the named laureates support?

Who should be the third B067 laureate beside Crews and Deshaies, Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structures, rational design) or Handa (cereblon identification), and what evidence should decide it?
Does the absence of an approved degrader make recognition premature in 2026, and what clinical or mechanistic evidence, if any, would change that judgement for Somfai, Brzezinski and Sparr?

For members who rank B067 first or second, what additional condition, if any, would move them to support it as the preferred prize part: Brzezinski, Somfai and Sparr, who list it as an alternative, are asked what specifically keeps it from being their first choice.

Can the B049 citation be written narrowly enough (liquid-like demixing as an organizing mechanism, not every reported condensate) to survive the overexpression-artefact critique, and if so, which three names, Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, or Pappu or Mittag in place of Rosen?
What exactly is distinct about C-N coupling (B013) relative to the 2010 prize, and does it open anything not already routine, in the terms Somfai and the critics have each put?
Is a two-part prize (as in Brzezinski's B069 plus B052 proposal) preferable to a single unified prize, and if so which pairings are coherent and do not exceed three laureates in total?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality-to-majority core on B067: five of eight members state it as their preferred prize part, but they split on the third name (Ciulli in four configurations, Handa in one) and on whether the citation reaches the glue branch. The three remaining members each hold a different first choice (B013, B049, and B069 with B052), and each lists at least one reservation about its maturity or novelty. Several members raise the same two concerns about B067 (no approved drug, credit spread across PROTAC and glue strands), so round 2 should resolve those rather than re-argue the principle. As chair I should record that my own round-1 configuration is B067 although my earlier first-place candidate was B049, and that members cited that earlier preference in several responses.
